entries.title: Two characters who share a surname were filed as one person: the King's tags overwrote the princess's record (The Princess, t85 and t89; found by the Thursday read, 2026-10-01).
entries.originalStatus: ◉ **Built v1.1097.** ONE veto in the one consolidation scan, `npcKeptApart` (memory.js): a name is never matched to a record it contradicts. Three contradictions count: sex (a title in the name, the record's pronouns, or the pronouns the same reply states for the name), age (old against young), and a crown's generation when only the surname is shared (the king beside Prince Aldric Underbough; "King Aldric" is still the same man, crowned). Nothing else changes: no signal, or the same signal, consolidates as before, and a registered alias or an exact name always wins. A title word that is the person's surname ("Marla King") and someone else's title ("the Queen's Champion Aldric") are not read as claims. The `[NPC:]` and `[NPC_PRONOUN:]` handlers say it once in the turn summary: "⚠ King Underbough is not Wilhelmina Underbough (he, not she) — filed as a separate person". **Proof:** 11 tests (8 red first); `dev/sabotage-503-npc-kept-apart.js` 23/23; the owner's save replayed in memory with its own t85 tags (shipped engine: one record, her pronouns flipped; fixed: two records); the full suite; the four replays, three unchanged and v1271's end state regenerated because its turn-1 fusion is gone (the whole change is "Refugee man" as his own row and the woman's mood and pronouns restored). The prompt is untouched. **Not repaired:** records already fused in a save. **Left open:** #504. Owner check: none needed; in play, a second family member under a title now appears as their own row in the character list.
